narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the organization has decided to deny your promotion.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your profile. Your total years of experience across all jobs was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. With 6–10 years overall, you sit in a group where many employees start considering new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay who have only 1–5 years of total experience. Your length of time in this current role (1–5 years) was the third most influential factor and also pulled the prediction toward leaving, as most employees who stay tend to have either very short or much longer tenure here.

Working in your favor, the second most important factor was that you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities pulled the prediction back toward staying. However, it was not enough to outweigh the combined influence of your experience levels.

The organization should review whether your current role is providing enough growth and challenge for someone with your background. You may want to discuss clear promotion pathways or new responsibilities that could increase your sense of progress and commitment. Addressing these points could help retain talented employees like you who are otherwise at risk of leaving. (218 words)
